topic-216-who-experiences-large-model-de.evolution: A 2006 method corrects selection bias by matching feature distributions through weights. Adaptive risk minimization in 2021 trains models explicitly to adapt using unlabeled test examples. Later representatives benchmark temporal shifts and monitor risk; TiME in 2026 studies transport-based expert routing to balance adaptation and stability across changing language-model domains.
openQuestions: How can a model detect that test-time adaptation is making performance worse?
Which information should be retained when domains recur after long intervals?
topic-216-who-experiences-large-model-de.overview: Models deployed on changing data may need to adapt using unlabeled observations from their new environment. This topic studies sample reweighting, learned adaptation rules, continual adjustment, and monitoring of adaptation risks. The central tension is improving performance on current inputs without destabilizing previously useful behavior or reinforcing incorrect predictions.
topic-216-who-experiences-large-model-de.title: Test-Time Adaptation and Distribution-Shift Monitoring
topic-216-who-experiences-large-model-de.whyItMatters: Test-time information can reveal shifts that training data cannot anticipate, but adapting is itself a source of error. A useful system must recognize when adjustment is supported by evidence, account for heterogeneous users or domains, and measure performance over time rather than only on one static shifted dataset.

topic-217-a-classification-based-study-o.evolution: Generative adversarial nets in 2014 formulate a two-player minimax game. Subsequent work modifies divergences, augmentation, and latent optimization. A 2019 approach uses task-dependent discrepancy for generators and ensembles; adversarial flow models in 2026 encourage deterministic noise-to-data transport while supporting one-step and multi-step generation through adversarial training.
openQuestions: Which discrepancies predict whether synthetic data will help a particular downstream task?
How can efficient adversarial generators preserve rare modes as well as common patterns?
topic-217-a-classification-based-study-o.overview: Adversarial generators learn by competing with a model that distinguishes generated data from observations. This topic studies the distance or discrepancy that competition minimizes, how to stabilize training, and how to work with limited data. Related approaches connect adversarial objectives with moment matching, ensembles, and flow-based generation.
topic-217-a-classification-based-study-o.title: Adversarial Generative Modeling and Distribution Matching
topic-217-a-classification-based-study-o.whyItMatters: The discriminator supplies a learned training signal, but the choice of objective determines which distributional differences matter. A generator useful for downstream learning may need task-sensitive fidelity rather than only visually convincing examples, and fast sampling must be considered alongside diversity and training stability.

topic-218-bf-textrmflow-differentiable-s.evolution: NeuroAnimator in 1998 learns to emulate physics-based animation models from simulated trajectories. Later representatives develop interaction networks and operators for partial differential equations. Recent work scales transformer solvers; a 2026 study combines neighborhood-level prediction, temporal correction, and geometric biases to improve accuracy and stability across several simulation architectures.
openQuestions: Which conservation and consistency constraints are essential for reliable long-horizon simulation?
How can operator models transfer to unfamiliar geometries without extensive new simulation data?
topic-218-bf-textrmflow-differentiable-s.overview: Learned simulators approximate how physical systems evolve, potentially replacing expensive numerical computations. This topic includes graph-based dynamics, neural operators, mesh-independent representations, and models shared across physical domains. Effective learning must respect spatial relationships and temporal evolution rather than merely fit isolated field values.
topic-218-bf-textrmflow-differentiable-s.title: Neural Operators and Learned Physical Simulation
topic-218-bf-textrmflow-differentiable-s.whyItMatters: Fast predictions are valuable for animation, engineering, and repeated simulation, but small local errors can grow during long rollouts. Generalization across meshes, geometries, and boundary conditions is therefore as important as accuracy on familiar snapshots. Numerical structure offers constraints that can improve stability and transfer.

topic-219-high-dimensional-structured-qu.evolution: Earlier representatives concern likelihood fitting and cross-validation. Recent work focuses on calibration, selection bias, and post-prediction analysis. PSPS in 2024 provides a task-agnostic framework for integrating predicted outcomes with established analyses; a 2026 adaptive-inference method combines predictions and labeled bandit data with asymptotic guarantees under conditions on the collection policy.
openQuestions: When can predictions improve inferential efficiency without adding hidden selection bias?
How should uncertainty account for repeated adaptation of both models and sampling policies?
topic-219-high-dimensional-structured-qu.overview: Machine-learning predictions can fill gaps in expensive or incomplete observations, but treating those predictions as measured truth can invalidate statistical conclusions. This topic combines predictive models with inference procedures that account for their errors, selection bias, and adaptive data collection. It also examines how evaluation can reveal unreliable estimates or forecasts.
topic-219-high-dimensional-structured-qu.title: Prediction-Assisted Statistical Inference and Evaluation
topic-219-high-dimensional-structured-qu.whyItMatters: The aim is to extract useful information from abundant unlabeled data without sacrificing valid uncertainty statements. Better prediction does not automatically guarantee unbiased scientific inference, especially when the data were selected adaptively or the target population differs from the observed sample.

topic-220-a-complete-recipe-for-stochast.evolution: A 1997 reversible-jump method samples Gaussian mixtures with an unknown component count. Later work develops manifold and Hamiltonian dynamics and stochastic-gradient recipes. Scalable Metropolis-Hastings in 2019 reduces average data processing while preserving the target posterior; a 2026 auxiliary-variable framework unifies methods for targets that are difficult even to evaluate.
openQuestions: How can practitioners assess exploration when exact target evaluations are unavailable?
Which geometric or auxiliary-variable constructions improve mixing without excessive per-step work?
topic-220-a-complete-recipe-for-stochast.overview: Monte Carlo inference explores a probability distribution through random transitions or weighted samples. This topic develops methods that exploit geometry, auxiliary variables, subsampling, and adaptive proposals to make Bayesian computation practical. It distinguishes algorithms with the correct invariant distribution from approximations whose computational savings introduce persistent bias.
topic-220-a-complete-recipe-for-stochast.title: Scalable Monte Carlo and Structured Bayesian Sampling
topic-220-a-complete-recipe-for-stochast.whyItMatters: Exactness is a property of the sampling construction, not a guarantee that a short run has explored the posterior adequately. Practical inference must also consider mixing, per-step cost, and diagnostics, especially when target evaluations are expensive or the number of model parameters can change.

topic-221-a-cognac-shot-to-forget-bad-me.evolution: Early representatives analyze prediction on weighted graphs and trust leakage. GNNGuard in 2020 reweights and prunes connections using relationships between features and structure. Later benchmarks reassess defenses at scale; a 2026 link-stealing study emphasizes success under very low false-positive rates, showing why average privacy metrics can miss concentrated vulnerabilities.
openQuestions: How can robustness defenses preserve informative connections between dissimilar nodes?
Which evaluations capture privacy risks concentrated in a small set of sensitive links?
topic-221-a-cognac-shot-to-forget-bad-me.overview: Graph models depend on relationships as well as node attributes, creating distinctive vulnerabilities. Small edge changes can disrupt predictions, while model outputs can reveal sensitive links. This topic studies defenses, robustness evaluation, uncertainty, and ownership protection, with attention to how information propagates through relational structure.
topic-221-a-cognac-shot-to-forget-bad-me.title: Graph Robustness, Privacy, and Trustworthy Learning
topic-221-a-cognac-shot-to-forget-bad-me.whyItMatters: Protecting a graph predictor requires specifying what an adversary can observe or modify. Average attack success can conceal severe exposure of a few important relationships, and a defense based on neighbor similarity must account for graphs where connected nodes legitimately differ. Evaluation needs to match these structural assumptions.

topic-222-h-consistency-bounds-for-pairw.evolution: A 1997 approach separates preference learning from approximate ordering. Later work studies ranking metrics, pairwise sample efficiency, and active elicitation under probabilistic models. In 2026, DMLRank uses debiased machine learning to estimate flexible ranking scores from human preferences, accommodate ties, and inform budget-constrained collection of additional comparisons.
openQuestions: How should ranking uncertainty be communicated when adjacent items are statistically indistinguishable?
Which comparison policies remain informative when preferences vary across users or contexts?
topic-222-h-consistency-bounds-for-pairw.overview: Ranking converts incomplete comparisons into an ordering of items, documents, or models. This topic studies how to learn preference functions, choose informative comparisons, optimize ranking metrics, and quantify uncertainty. Pairwise judgments need not be perfectly consistent, so recovering an ordering involves both statistical modeling and combinatorial choices.
topic-222-h-consistency-bounds-for-pairw.title: Learning to Rank from Noisy Preferences
topic-222-h-consistency-bounds-for-pairw.whyItMatters: A leaderboard or retrieval list can appear definitive even when supported by sparse, noisy, or context-dependent preferences. Reliable ranking methods should expose uncertainty and allocate comparison budgets carefully. The appropriate objective may prioritize the best few items rather than agreement across every possible pair.

topic-223-efficient-black-box-adversaria.evolution: Houdini in 2017 targets task-level performance measures for structured outputs. Later representatives explore limited-query attacks, visible patches, adversarial training, and generative purification. A 2026 visual-injection defense uses hidden-state gradient attribution to identify and suppress critical image tokens, reporting strong protection within its tested multimodal attack settings.
openQuestions: How can defenses remain effective when attackers adapt to the defense itself?
Which evaluations jointly measure preserved task utility and resistance to multimodal manipulation?
topic-223-efficient-black-box-adversaria.overview: Adversarial inputs deliberately exploit a model’s sensitivities to alter its behavior. This topic studies attacks and defenses across images, speech, structured prediction, and vision-language systems, including visual prompt injection. Methods differ in available access, query budgets, perturbation constraints, and the task outcome they attempt to change.
topic-223-efficient-black-box-adversaria.title: Adversarial Examples and Multimodal Defense
topic-223-efficient-black-box-adversaria.whyItMatters: Robustness claims are meaningful only relative to a specified threat model and evaluation. A defense that handles familiar perturbations may fail against an adaptive adversary, while aggregate success rates can obscure utility losses. Studying attacks provides a way to test these boundaries systematically.
